family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid in which the order of the elements within each row is reversed, but the order of the rows themselves is unchanged. Rows may have different lengths, and an empty grid should produce an empty grid.
reference:
def reverse_rows_elements(grid):
    return [row[::-1] for row in grid]

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid in which the order of the rows is reversed (the first row becomes the last and vice versa), while the elements within each row stay in their original order. An empty grid should produce an empty grid.
reference:
def flip_vertical(grid):
    return grid[::-1]

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers and a threshold value, count how many cells in the grid contain a value strictly greater than the threshold. Negative thresholds and negative grid values are both allowed, and an empty grid should give a count of 0.
reference:
def count_greater_than(grid, threshold):
    return sum(1 for row in grid for v in row if v > threshold)

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a square 2D grid of integers, return the sum of all elements on its main diagonal plus all elements on its anti-diagonal. If the grid has an odd size, the single center cell (which lies on both diagonals) must be counted only once, not twice.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a square 2D grid of integers, determine whether it is a magic square: every row, every column, the main diagonal, and the anti-diagonal must all sum to the same total. An empty grid (zero rows) counts as a magic square.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of 0s and 1s, where 0 marks an open cell and 1 marks a blocked obstacle, count the number of distinct paths from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell that move only right or down at each step, without ever entering a blocked cell. If the starting cell or the destination cell is itself blocked, return 0.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid containing only the integers 0 and 1, count the number of separate islands, where an island is a group of 1-cells connected to each other horizontally or vertically (not diagonally). If the grid contains no 1-cells, or the grid is empty, return 0.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, a starting row sr, a starting column sc, and a new value, perform a flood fill: replace the value at (sr, sc) and every cell reachable from it through horizontally or vertically adjacent cells of the same original value with the new value, and return the resulting grid as a new grid (the input grid must not be modified). If the new value is the same as the value already at (sr, sc), return a copy of the grid unchanged.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return the number of distinct values that appear anywhere in the grid. An empty grid, or a grid whose rows are all empty, has 0 distinct values.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a square 2D grid of integers, return the trace of the matrix, defined as the sum of the elements on its main diagonal (grid[0][0] + grid[1][1] + ... ). An empty grid (zero rows) has a trace of 0.
reference:
def matrix_trace(grid):
    return sum(grid[i][i] for i in range(len(grid)))

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, determine whether it looks identical after being rotated 180 degrees, meaning grid[i][j] equals grid[rows-1-i][cols-1-j] for every cell. Return True if this holds for every cell (including for an empty grid), and False otherwise.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return the sum of the values of all cells that lie on the border of the grid (the first row, the last row, the first column, or the last column). If the grid has only one row or one column, every cell counts as a border cell. Return 0 if the grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers and two values old and new, return a new grid (the input grid must not be modified) in which every cell equal to old has been replaced by new, and all other cells are unchanged. If old never appears in the grid, the returned grid must have the same values as the input.
reference:
def replace_value(grid, old, new):
    return [[new if v == old else v for v in row] for row in grid]

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, count how many of its rows read the same forwards and backwards (are palindromes). A row with zero or one elements always counts as a palindrome. An empty grid has 0 palindromic rows.
reference:
def count_palindrome_rows(grid):
    return sum(1 for row in grid if row == row[::-1])

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, count how many of its columns, read from top to bottom, read the same forwards and backwards (are palindromes). A column with zero or one elements always counts as a palindrome. Return 0 if the grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given two 2D grids of integers a and b representing matrices, where a has dimensions m by n and b has dimensions n by p, return their matrix product as a new m by p grid, computed using standard matrix multiplication. Assume the number of columns of a always matches the number of rows of b.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers and a target value, return a tuple (row, col) giving the position of the first cell (scanning row by row, left to right) whose value equals the target. If the target value does not appear anywhere in the grid, return None.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers with at least one row and one column, return the sum of the values at its four corners: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. If the grid has only one row or one column, some corners coincide with each other, but each of the four corner positions must still be added, so a coinciding value is counted more than once.
reference:
def corner_sum(grid):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    return grid[0][0] + grid[0][cols - 1] + grid[rows - 1][0] + grid[rows - 1][cols - 1]

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, determine whether its values form a checkerboard pattern, meaning every cell differs from each of its horizontally and vertically adjacent neighbours, with exactly two distinct values used alternately based on whether the sum of a cell's row and column index is even or odd. A grid with a single cell, or an empty grid, counts as a valid checkerboard.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers and a non-negative integer k, return a new grid in which the rows have been cyclically shifted downward by k positions, so that a row that would shift past the bottom reappears at the top. The shift amount k may be larger than the number of rows, in which case it should wrap around (use k modulo the number of rows). An empty grid always returns an empty grid.
